meta.method: Each event checked against at least two independent web reports (news, regulator or court documents) via web search. Figures for move size differ between outlets; ranges are given where they differ. Fields listed in unverified_fields could not be confirmed and should not be cited as fact.
corrections_to_brief: Tariff pause hoax occurred on 2025-04-07 (not 9 April).
Emulex drop: SEC figure is about 58% ($103.94 to $43.00); the 62% figure appears only in secondary sources.

events.time: about 1:07 pm ET (reported variously 1:07-1:08); recovery by about 1:13-1:18 pm ET
events.published: Tweet from hacked @AP account: breaking news that two explosions at the White House had injured the President.
events.asset: US equity indices (Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500), Treasuries, crude oil
events.move: Dow fell about 143 points (14,697 to 14,554) per AP wire; other outlets say 125-145. About 0.9-1.0 percent. Reports of about USD 136 billion S&P 500 value erased come from a single secondary roundup.
events.correction: AP said account was hacked and suspended; White House spokesman Jay Carney said the President was fine. Syrian Electronic Army claimed the hack; FBI investigated.

events.time: unverified (US morning session, shortly after 10 am ET in some accounts)
events.published: AI-generated image of smoke near the Pentagon, spread by verified accounts including one impersonating a news agency ("Bloomberg Feed") and shared by a Russian state media outlet, which later deleted it.
events.move: S&P 500 dipped about 0.26 percent briefly (one outlet cites about 30 points); a Briefing.com analyst said the decline was small relative to the nature of the news.
events.correction: Arlington County Fire Department posted that there was no explosion or incident at or near the Pentagon reservation.

events.time: morning ET, before 10:38 am ET denial by White House Rapid Response; exact start time unverified
events.published: Post claiming a senior White House economic adviser said the President was considering a 90-day tariff pause for all countries except China (a misreading of a TV interview). Originated with a small account, then relayed by a larger account that reposts terminal headlines, then by CNBC and Reuters headlines.
events.move: S&P 500 rose more than 6-7 percent intraday on the rumour (reports range 6-8 percent, Nasdaq about 10 percent swing) and gave up nearly all of it after denial.
events.duration: About 30 minutes up, reversal within minutes of denial
events.correction: White House press secretary called it fake news to CNBC; White House Rapid Response account denied; Reuters retracted its story, saying it relied on a CNBC headline; the posting account deleted the post.
unverified_fields: which account originated the claim (sources conflict)

events.time: about 4:11 pm ET (unverified in sources retrieved)
events.published: Post on the regulator's compromised X account announcing approval of spot bitcoin exchange-traded products.
events.move: BTC rose to about 47,600-47,870 from about 46,800, then fell to about 45,400-45,500. Roughly 2-3 percent each way. Liquidations of about USD 90 million reported by one outlet.
events.correction: The regulator's chair posted that the account was compromised and no approval had been given; X said a phone number was taken over via a third party (SIM swap). Real approval followed on 2024-01-10.

events.time: unverified (US morning; exact minute not confirmed)
events.published: "BREAKING: SEC APPROVES ISHARES BITCOIN SPOT ETF", posted by a crypto news outlet's social team from an unconfirmed screenshot attributed to a terminal.
events.move: BTC rose from about 27,700 to about 29,900-30,000 (roughly 5-10 percent, depending on outlet), then fell to about 28,000. Liquidations reported at USD 81-100 million.
events.correction: Asset manager spokesperson said application was still under review; reporters confirmed; the outlet deleted the post, apologised and opened an internal investigation.

events.published: Press release on a newswire stating a retailer would accept Litecoin for online payments from October 1.
events.move: LTC rose from about 175 to about 230-240 USD (roughly 30-35 percent), then reversed.
events.duration: Minutes up, reversal within about an hour
events.correction: Retailer said it had no knowledge of the release; Litecoin's creator confirmed it was fake; newswire said a fraudulent user account issued it, withdrew it and issued a disregard notice.

events.time: unverified (afternoon ET; tweet stayed up for hours)
events.published: "We are excited to announce insulin is free now" from a paid-verified account impersonating a drugmaker.
events.asset: Eli Lilly (LLY) equity; to a lesser degree other insulin makers
events.move: LLY fell about 4.4-4.5 percent on the day (about USD 368 to 346). Causality is uncertain: sources note the fall may reflect the broader publicity or other factors; the company declined to attribute it.
events.correction: The real company apologised for the misleading message; the impersonating account was suspended and unverified.
unverified_fields: causal attribution of the stock move to the tweet

events.time: trading halted about 11:06-11:07 am ET, resumed 12:30 pm ET
events.published: A 2002 newspaper story about the airline's bankruptcy filing was re-indexed by a search aggregator with a new date, picked up by a financial news reporter and spread across terminals.
events.platform: Online newspaper site, search aggregator, financial news terminals
events.move: Intraday low about USD 3 (roughly 75 percent below prior close of about 12.3); closed at 10.92, down about 11-12 percent.
events.duration: About 1.5 hours to recover most of the loss; halt of about 80 minutes
events.correction: Company said story concerned its 2002 filing and demanded a retraction; newspaper acknowledged an old story; Nasdaq halted trading.

events.time: unverified in sources retrieved (about 3:00 pm Paris time per general recollection, not confirmed)
events.published: Fake press release imitating the company, claiming an internal audit found accounting irregularities, the finance chief would be dismissed and 2015 and half-year 2016 accounts restated; republished by a financial news service.
events.platform: Fake press release (look-alike domain), picked up by Bloomberg
events.move: Intraday fall about 18.3 percent (regulator cites 18.28), close down about 4 percent.
events.duration: Recovered most of the loss within the same session
events.correction: Company denied and called it a hoax; regulator fined the news service EUR 5 million in 2019 for disseminating false information (reduced to EUR 3 million on appeal in 2021).

events.time: 9:30 am EDT (release issued, per SEC); fall within about 16 minutes
events.published: Fake press release claiming the CEO had resigned, an SEC investigation was under way and earnings would be restated.
events.platform: Internet Wire (newswire), picked up by financial media
events.move: From USD 103.94 to 43.00 (about 58 percent) per SEC; secondary sources say 62 percent. About USD 2.2 billion of market value lost.
events.duration: Trading halted; stock recovered the same day, closing at 105.75
events.correction: Company called it categorically false; Nasdaq halted trading; the perpetrator, a former wire employee who had bought shares, was prosecuted, pleaded guilty and was sentenced to 44 months.

events.time: unverified (US afternoon/evening; exact minute not confirmed)
events.published: Post from the compromised official account of a head of state saying bitcoin had become legal tender, a USD 5 million bitcoin reserve approved, and urging readers to buy via a wallet address.
events.move: BTC rose about 4 percent to a local high of about 110,450; sources note concurrent US-China trade-talk news also contributed, so attribution to the post is partial.
events.correction: The presidency flagged unauthorised access; post deleted; national cyber incident team and X restored control.
unverified_fields: share of the move attributable to the post
